national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that India supports a safe, secure, peaceful and sustainable space domain anchored in international law, dialogue and multilateral cooperation. He said India’s approach is rooted in Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, that is One Earth, One Family, One Future, and this spirit must now travel beyond Earth. The Prime Minister was virtually addressing the International Space Summit in Paris today. He said scientific data must serve the common good, with openness and integrity. The Prime Minister stressed that cooperation over confrontation, sustainability over short-term gain and inclusion over exclusion must be prioritised as orbits become more crowded and actors more numerous. He said, for centuries, space inspired our imagination and today it shapes life on Earth, from climate and crops to oceans and communities. He said, the promise of space is infinite. Highlighting the remarkable growth of country’s space journey, Mr. Modi said Chandrayan-3 made India the first nation to land near the lunar south pole and Aditya-L1 is unlocking the secrets of the Sun. He said, an Indian visited the International Space Station last year. He said, India aims to establish an Indian space station by 2035 and send an Indian to the Moon by 2040. He said, country’s guiding principle is clear their benefits must reach all humanity. Lauding the role of ISRO in space journey, Mr. Modi said ISRO has earned global admiration for its excellence and cost-effective missions. He said, its capabilities serve farmers and fishermen, weather forecasting, disaster management and navigation and more than 430 satellites from 34 countries have travelled to space aboard Indian rockets. He said, ISRO’s technologies and partnerships serve not only India, but the wider world. He appreciated the contribution, dedication and hard work of generations of Indian scientists, engineers and technicians. The Prime Minister said that ISRO has built its reputation mission by mission, success by success, and given India a place of pride among spacefaring nations.

national_raw_news.title: 50 mins ago | National 91 All preparations in full swing for two-day BRICS Summit 2026 beginning Saturday
national_raw_news.content: India is all set to host the 18th BRICS Summit beginning this Saturday at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The two day Summit will bring together eleven major emerging and developing economies, including Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, India, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, and the UAE. Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan, and Vietnam will participate as the BRICS Partner Countries. BRICS collectively represents around 49 per cent of the world’s population, and about 40 per cent of global GDP. World leaders including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, President of South Africa Cyril Ramaphosa, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian, and Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed al Nahyan will participate in the Summit. Prime Minister of Ethiopia Abiy Ahmed Ali will also participate. Brazil will be represented by Foreign Affairs Minister Mauro Vieira. Minister of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud will also participate in the Summit. The BRICS Summit 2026 will get underway on Saturday with a Closed Session for BRICS Member Countries on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism”. Leaders of BRICS Member Countries will witness the Bharat Innovates Exhibition at Bharat Mandapam. They will also undertake a joint tree plantation which will be followed by a Gala Dinner hosted by Prime Minister Modi. The Prime Minister is also expected to hold a series of bilateral meetings with BRICS leaders on the sidelines of the Summit. On Sunday, Mr Modi will welcome the Leaders of BRICS Partner Countries and Outreach Invitees. The Leaders will participate in a Session on “Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth”. Our correspondent reports that preparations are underway in full swing ahead of the BRICS Summit 2026. The national capital is all decked up to welcome world leaders for the Summit, with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping expected to touch down in Delhi tomorrow. It has been a large logistical exercise with the Ministry of External Affairs closely coordinating with other Ministries including Home Ministry, as well as Delhi Police. The Delhi Police has made made elaborate arrangements in order to ensure maximum security for visiting dignitaries while causing minimum inconvenience to the public. Around 15 thousand Delhi Police Personnel and 200 companies of paramilitary forces have been deployed in the national capital. Special Commissioner of Police, Protective Security Division, Manish Kumar Agrawal said that Specialised surveillance cameras have also been deployed along routes to be used by visiting dignitaries. India’s Chairship is centred on the four pillars of the theme – Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. Since assuming the Chairship, over 350 meetings have been held including the Meeting of BRICS Ministers of Foreign Affairs, BRICS National Security Advisers, Ministerial Meetings, Sherpa and Head of Agency level Meetings, Working Group level Meetings, and P2P & B2B engagements.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 21 India and Russia step forward on joint production of civil passenger planes
national_raw_news.content: India and Russia today held talks on joint production of civil passenger planes, and potential deliveries and arrangements for 105 regional turboprop aircraft to Indian operators. India’s Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu held discussions with Russia’s Industry and Trade Minister Anton Alikhanov on joint manufacturing of civil passenger aircraft to meet country’s demand for regional air connectivity, in New Delhi. Discussions and proposed deals also cover potential deliveries and arrangements for 105 regional turboprop aircraft to Indian operators, including Pinnacle Air, Air Kerala, and Sleek Aviation. Russia also displayed its regional SJ-100, MC-21, and Il-114-300 aircraft at the Innoprom event in New Delhi to target India’s expanding regional connectivity needs. Public sector aerospace company Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd. (HAL) and Russia’s United Aircraft Corporation (UAC) previously signed an initial agreement for the licensed joint production and support of the Superjet (SJ-100) civil commuter aircraft in India. Talking to the media, Mr Naidu said that he had a discussion with the delegation regarding the progress of MoU that HAL had with Russia in terms of manufacturing a plane in the country. Regarding the Civil Aviation Requirement (CAR) draft on pilot testing, the Minister said that Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is having discussions with different stakeholders and according to the discussions new guidelines on the pilot testing will be finalized by the end of this month. In a social media post, Mr Naidu said that with the immense potential of regional connectivity, there is a strong opportunity for India and Russia to take bilateral relationship from buyer-seller to joint manufacturing and deeper industrial cooperation. He said that India-Russia ties continue to grow, with aviation emerging as a key pillar of the strategic partnership. The growing aviation engagement comes as Russia seeks to deepen industrial cooperation with India beyond traditional defence platforms such as the MiG and Sukhoi fighter jets. The proposed aircraft deals indicate a possible expansion of India-Russia aerospace ties into civil aviation, regional connectivity and aircraft manufacturing. The two-day ‘Innoprom India’, began yesterday in New Delhi ahead of the BRICS summit, has brought together more than 120 Russian and Indian companies.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 28 Centre amends e-commerce rules to protect consumers and enhance transparency
national_raw_news.content: The government has amended the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020, to tighten norms on price transparency, sponsored listings, search result manipulation and dark patterns. Under the amended rules, e-commerce entities will have to disclose the reduced price and prior price whenever a price cut is announced. The prior price has been defined as the lowest price at which the product was offered in the 30 days before the discount was announced. The rules bar e-commerce entities from manipulating search results that mislead users or affect the relevance of results to a search query. The amended rules will establish a more transparent, accountable and consumer-centric e-commerce ecosystem. The amended rules will come into force from 1st January next year. The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution said that the amended rules will strengthen the ease of doing business by curtailing safety issues around digital marketplace. It also highlighted that every e-commerce entity will be required to become a partner in the convergence process of the National Consumer Helpline providing an inclusive grievance redressal mechanism. Under the new rules, every e-commerce entity shall provide the complainant with a copy of the complaint as recorded by its grievance officer. E-commerce entities will not manipulate search results in a manner that misleads users or adversely affects the relevance of results to the user’s search query. Importer details and country of origin shall be disclosed for imported goods.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 38 HM Amit Shah calls for disaster-resilient villages and cities under zero-casualty vision
national_raw_news.content: Home Minister Amit Shah today said that the Narendra Modi led government has completely transformed the country’s disaster management system and set the goal of zero casualty. He was speaking while chairing the third meeting of the Governing Body of the National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) in New Delhi. Mr Shah said that the government is focusing on three pillars which are risk reduction, early warning systems and zero casualty. He stressed that the zero casualty approach should not be limited to disaster sites but should also focus on preventing disasters. The Home Minister said that over the last 12 years, there has been a comprehensive transformation in country’s approach and methodology towards disaster management. He highlighted initiatives such as Mission LiFE, Pro-Planet People and the International Solar Alliance as important contributions towards disaster prevention. He said the government’s goal is to create disaster-resilient villages and cities. Mr Shah said that the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) have responsibilities ranging from policymaking to training and implementation, keeping in view emerging disaster risks arising from global warming and climate change. He directed both institutions to study global research and implement relevant findings in India according to local requirements. He called for permanent preparedness to deal with locust swarm attacks originating from Pakistan and stressed the need to give priority to committed personnel in disaster management training. He also directed NDMA and NIDM to jointly issue nationwide guidelines specifying what should and should not be done during different types of disasters. The Minister emphasized the need for research to identify the causes of disasters and directed NDMA, NIDM, NDRF and SDRF to jointly study the causes of damage and prepare detailed reports. Mr Shah said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has decided that the distribution of disaster funds should also follow a scientific process. He noted that allocation under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) has increased nearly fourfold, while allocation under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) has increased nearly threefold. He also called for wider adoption of the disaster management mobile application in higher, secondary and primary education sectors. He directed all stakeholders to establish dedicated cells in their departments and asked department heads to review implementation every three months.

national_raw_news.title: India, Russia working towards achieving $100bn mark in bilateral trade by 2030: Piyush Goyal 15 mins ago 7
national_raw_news.content: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has called for an accelerated India-Russia economic and industrial partnership, with both countries working towards achieving hundred billion US dollar mark in bilateral trade and 50 billion dollars in two-way investment by 2030. Addressing the INNOPROM India 2026 Co-Chair Plenary Session with Russian Minister of Industry and Trade Anton Alikhanov in New Delhi today, Mr Goyal said that the targets set by the two Heads of State would measure the performance of governments and businesses of both countries. He said that country’s exports including aquatic products, vegetables, coffee, tea, spices and milling products to Russia have increased significantly. On investment, Mr Goyal said that the India-Russia priority investment projects mechanism is tracking 40 live projects in advanced manufacturing, energy, mining, railways and emerging technologies. He urged Russia to facilitate greater Indian investment in pharmaceuticals, IT, artificial intelligence, services, engineering and railways. Mr Goyal said that the two countries are fast-tracking a new bilateral investment treaty to provide greater legal certainty to investors. He also said that India and the Eurasian Economic Union have begun formal free trade negotiations, with India committing to concluding them early to open new markets, particularly for MSMEs. On the occasion, he also stressed the need to strengthen national and local currency payment mechanisms and improve connectivity through the International North-South Transport Corridor and Chennai-Vladivostok maritime corridor. Mr goyal said that the India-Russia relationship has withstood seven decades of global change. He described the first-ever presence of INNOPROM in India as a significant step towards moving from protocols to production and from intent to industry.

national_raw_news.title: Creative economy reforms help to protect producers from privacy, says MoS Dr. L. Murugan 7 mins ago 4
national_raw_news.content: Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr. L. Murugan today said that the government is making efforts to create two million professionals by building the necessary infrastructure, while creative economy reforms are helping protect producers from piracy. He was addressing at the valedictory function of International Film Festival of Jammu and Kashmir. The Minister said the festival is a translation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision, who had invited filmmakers to shoot and make films in Kashmir in 2019. Congratulating the Jammu and Kashmir Government for organising the festival, Dr. Murugan said the festival belongs to the youth of Jammu and Kashmir and that the youth are proving that imagination knows no boundaries. Later Mr. Murugan also gave award for best film from J&K select section, Tasrufdaar (The Djinns of Kashmir). Secretary of Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Chanchal Kumar was also present on the occasion. He congratulated the Jammu and Kashmir Government for bringing together filmmakers and cinema professionals. He said Jammu and Kashmir has given iconic films to Indian cinema and hosting the festival has opened a new chapter in the history of the region. Chanchal Kumar said the Ministry is creating opportunities for young talent through platforms such as the WAVES Summit. Referring to the Film Bazaar, he said filmmakers from Jammu and Kashmir can benefit by connecting with buyers and the wider film market. He also mentioned the Indian Institute of Creative Technology being developed by the Ministry and invited the youth of Jammu and Kashmir to explore the film market and acquire new skills. He said the Ministry and the Jammu and Kashmir Government can work together to create more opportunities for young filmmakers and creators from the region.
